subject: Retention policy — default capture vs generated outputs: mapping & exceptions
messages:
From: Ellen Murray <ellen.murray@aureliahealth.org>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@aureliahealth.org
Date: 2025-08-19 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Sergio,

We're finalizing our vendor assessment and need a concise mapping: for Redwood's hosted API, by default which elements are retained vs ephemeral? Specifically: 1) raw request (user prompt), 2) intermediate model state/stream fragments, 3) final generated output, 4) embeddings and logs derived from responses.

Aurelia's InfoSec needs this in plain language (we'll paste into our spreadsheet), plus examples of any exceptions (e.g., attachments, debugging traces, exports). Also let me know whether there's a straightforward way for us to request deletion of a specific conversation and what evidence you provide.

Thanks — tight timelines on this review, so a short, clear reply would be great.

—Ellen
Ellen Murray
Head of Information Security
Aurelia Health
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Murray <ellen.murray@aureliahealth.org>
Date: 2025-08-19 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear ask. TL;DR ringfence below, then attaching a simple matrix and a few examples. If you want this copy-paste-ready for your vendor spreadsheet let me know and I'll send a one-paragraph summary.

What Redwood retains by default (hosted API):
- Raw request (user prompt): typically retained as a request record when a customer opts into analytics or uses persistent logs; for strict ephemeral sessions (session mode) requests can be excluded by configuration.
- Stream fragments / intermediate model state: considered transient by default. Streaming buffers are not persisted to long-term stores unless explicit debug capture is enabled.
- Final generated output: stored by default as a response artifact to enable billing, debugging, and quality monitoring; customers can opt-out per-route or request a deletion.
- Embeddings / derived artifacts: treated as customer-owned artifacts and stored; they are covered by the same retention controls and can be deleted on request.

Exceptions and notes:
- Attachments referenced in requests (files uploaded to the service) are retained according to the attachments retention policy and are included in erasure requests.
- Debug traces and verbose logs: only captured when the customer enables debug mode or when an incident triggers deeper capture; not on by default.
- EU/region-specific residency: data stored in-region when customer chooses regional deployment; deletion proofs reflect the residency store.

Deletion path: submit a deletion request via the Console or support portal; we provide an execution ticket and erasure evidence (time-stamped runbook entry and storage object IDs) once the deletion pipeline completes. Typical turnaround is 48–72 hours for standard requests.

Attaching: retention-default-matrix-v1.pdf and a small CSV with capture examples. Looping in our policy owner (cc).

Best,
Sergio

Sergio — quick clarifications to use in customer-facing replies: please use these exact bullets so procurement teams see consistent wording.

- Default capture: Requests (user inputs) and final outputs are stored by default for hosted customers to support billing, abuse detection, and quality monitoring.
- Transient items: Streaming fragments and ephemeral KV cache contents are not persisted to long-term storage by default and are excluded from retention proofs unless debug capture or a support-led incident capture was enabled.
- Derived artifacts: Embeddings and indexes created via our APIs are considered persisted customer artifacts and follow the customer's retention window; they are deletable on request.
- Attachments & uploads: Files uploaded via our attachment endpoints are stored and covered by the same deletion pipeline; we surface a file ID in the erasure evidence.
- Deletion SLA: For hosted accounts, we aim to complete standard erasure requests within 72 hours; for Dedicated or Private deployments SLAs are contract-specific.
- Evidence provided: time-stamped deletion ticket, storage object IDs or database row IDs, and a short runbook note. For customers requiring formal attestation we can provide signed deletion statements under enterprise agreements.

Ben — flagging anything else I should add for legal/regulatory nuance (PII vs non-PII handling).

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Privacy & Compliance

Hi Ellen — short, vendor-spreadsheet friendly summary below (you can paste this directly):

- Requests (user prompts): Stored by default for hosted accounts to enable billing and quality monitoring. Can be excluded via session/ephemeral configuration.
- Streaming/intermediate fragments: Transient by default; not written to long-term stores unless debug capture or incident collection is enabled.
- Final outputs (model answers): Persisted by default; deletable via the Console or support with erasure evidence.
- Embeddings/derived artifacts: Persisted and customer-owned; covered by retention controls and deletable on request.
- Attachments/uploads: Persisted; included in deletion requests and referenced by file ID in evidence.

Deletion logistics: file a request in the Console or open a support ticket. Typical hosted turnaround is up to 72 hours; dedicated/private timelines are contract-specific. We provide deletion ticket ID, time-stamped evidence and storage object IDs.

Attaching the retention matrix and a few examples for your spreadsheet. If Aurelia needs a signed attestation for erasure we can route through our enterprise compliance team — happy to introduce.

Best regards,
